title: Identification of Potentially Pathogenic Missense nsSNPs of Erythroid Krüppel-like Factor (EKLF) Gene Using In Silico Analysis and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
content: Background/Objectives: Krüppel-like factor 1 (KLF1) is an erythroid-specific transcription factor essential for erythropoiesis and globin gene regulation. This study aimed to identify potentially deleterious KLF1 missense variants and investigate their structural and functional consequences using integrated computational analyses. Methods: A total of 488 missense variants were initially screened for their deleterious effect using SIFT, PROVEAN, and PolyPhen-2. Disease association was predicted using SNPs&GO and PhD-SNP, while protein stability was assessed using I-Mutant2.0 and MUpro. MutPred2 predicted molecular alterations, ConSurf evaluated evolutionary conservation, and InterPro identified functional domains. Project HOPE examined structural and physicochemical changes, whereas DynaMut assessed intramolecular interactions and protein flexibility. Selected variants underwent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) to investigate conformational behavior. Results: Of the 488 variants, 80 were predicted to be deleterious, 48 were classified as disease-associated, and 37 were predicted to reduce protein stability. MutPred2 identified nine variants with significant predicted molecular alterations. Conservation and structural analyses highlighted R350 and G335 as important residues within the DNA-binding region. MDS of four selected variants (R350L, R350P, R350C, and G335R) revealed the greatest conformational deviations, increased flexibility, reduced compactness, and fewer hydrogen bonds in R350C. G335R exhibited increased compactness and altered intramolecular interactions, whereas R350L showed limited structural changes. Conclusions: R350C and G335R emerged as priority variants for further functional investigation, suggesting distinct mechanisms of KLF1 dysfunction. Experimental studies are essential to determine whether the predicted structural alterations affect DNA binding, transcriptional activity, and erythroid function, and to establish their clinical relevance to KLF1-associated hematological disorders.
